## LineCableModels Workbench

The workbench is a standalone Bonito route rather than a widget embedded in this document. It owns navigation, commands, persistent workspace views, the inspector, a resizable output dock, and the status bar.

Its demonstration is deliberately local: no broker connection, worker, numerical operation, or domain package is constructed when the page opens.

[Open the full workbench →](/workbenches/template){.lc-workbench-open}

## Owned-component X-ray

Start the publisher with component diagnostics enabled:

```bash
./lcm playground start --xray
```

Hover an owned component to inspect its Julia type, configured parameters,
live bindings, typed actions, source definition, rendered dimensions, and only
the CSS rules declared for that component's registered selector scopes. Drag
the inspector by its header or resize it from the lower-right corner. Click to
pin the inspection, use its breadcrumb to select an owned ancestor, press
`Escape` to release it, or toggle the mode with `Ctrl+Shift+X`.

X-ray metadata is not emitted unless the server is started with `--xray`.
:::

## Reuse without copying the shell

Global structural primitives and rendering live in:

```text
src/workbench/WorkbenchUI.jl
src/workbench/workbench.css
```

The self-contained specialization is:

```text
src/workbenches/TemplateWorkbench.jl
src/workbenches/template_workbench.css
```

A new application defines session state, composes the semantic regions, and implements typed `handle!` methods. It does not reproduce the shell DOM or global styling.
:::

:::

## Narrow extension contract

```julia
struct CableStudy <: AbstractWorkbench end

initialize(::CableStudy, session) = StudyState(...)

compose(::CableStudy, state) = Workbench(
    namespace = :cable_study,
    identity = Identity(...),
    navigation = Sidebar(...),
    workspace = ViewStack(...),
    inspector = Inspector(...),
    output = Dock(...),
    status = StatusBar(...),
)

handle!(::CableStudy, state, ::FitView) = fit!(state.viewport)
```

Views and actions are ordinary Julia types. Domain modules extend their behavior through dispatch; DOM identity is generated per browser session.

The workspace accepts reusable two-way splits directly. Splits may be nested;
the leaves remain ordinary view or DOM values:

```julia
workspace = SplitPane(
    scene,
    SplitPane(inputs, results; orientation=:vertical, ratio=0.45);
    orientation=:horizontal,
    ratio=0.72,
)
```
